Are these the three possible OData types? If Yes, does it makes sense to have them all inside a single object like  cloudConfig? I am thinking something like

```json
"triggerType": {
    "dataOdataTypeExpression": "@{triggerBody()?['data']?['@odata.type']}",
    "uploadDataType": "#microsoft.graph.customDataProvidedResourceRequestAccessReviewDataCalloutData",
    "applyDecisionType": "#microsoft.graph.customDataProvidedResourceApplyDecisionContextData",
    "updateAccessAssignmentType": "#microsoft.graph.customDataProvidedResourceAccessAssignmentCalloutData"
}
```

or 

```json
"dataOdataTypeExpression": "@{triggerBody()?['data']?['@odata.type']}",
"triggerType": {
    "uploadDataTriggerType": "#microsoft.graph.customDataProvidedResourceRequestAccessReviewDataCalloutData",
    "applyDecisionTriggerType": "#microsoft.graph.customDataProvidedResourceApplyDecisionContextData",
    "updateAccessAssignmentTriggerType": "#microsoft.graph.customDataProvidedResourceAccessAssignmentCalloutData"
}
```
API Versions should not be parameterized. Can this (and other instances of this) parameter be removed, and the API version can be hardcoded?

We have used API version in the parameters to allow extensibility to the customers.
If we remove this api version now, this would mean a breaking change for consumers at this point.
Would be to possible to allow us take in this in a planned manner in future iterations ?
API Version should not be parameterized

Why is the whole properties body being passed as a parameter value? The individual properties should be declared and then the values should be parameterized. If you want you can use an `object` parameter type if you only want one parameter, but as it is currently authored this is an anti-pattern that will be confusing for any consumer of this template.
